content.comment_body: Hello everyone, This is my first experience working with analogue outputs on [product_name]. I have a 4-20mA analogue input sensor connected, and an analogue amplifier is providing real-world values in the range of 0-440. I’d like to generate a 0-10V output, corresponding specifically to the amplified range 190-210 (e.g., 190 = 0V, 200 = 5V, 210 = 10V). My solution works so far, but it feels inelegant. I haven’t managed to restrict the output values between 0-1000, but, in practice, I don't think this will be an issue. Any advice is welcome. Thank you, [user_name]
Hello! Check out the attached file; I created a program that probably fits your requirements. Please share your thoughts!

Hello [user_name], [user_name] provided the logic plan that's needed. For future use, when calculating GAIN and OFFSET, you can see my method in the Scaling Question thread. To simplify calculations, I’ve made an Excel sheet for GAIN and OFFSET—see the attached file. Note: If your values exceed the operational range, you’ll require multiple amplifiers and must recalculate GAIN and OFFSET based on the new input values to each subsequent amplifier! Best regards, [user_name]

Hello all, I appreciate everyone's input. After some consideration, I realized my initial approach wasn’t ideal. It turns out that using a PI controller was the right solution. For those interested, here is the logic—it maintains pressure at 200Psi by adjusting the speed of a cooling fan. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed how to create a proportional analogue output based on a specific input range using [product_name], noting initial solutions were functional but could be improved. Community feedback, sample logic, and external tools (such as an Excel sheet for scaling calculations) helped refine approaches. Ultimately, the original poster revised their solution to use a PI controller for automatic control, highlighting the value of flexible control strategies and accessible support resources for related calculations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a simple and effective way to correlate analogue sensor input values to corresponding output voltages, including straightforward methods for output range restriction and calculation of scaling factors.
